messages.subject: Cross-lagged mediation code question
parts:
Hello, 

I'm running a cross-lagged panel model to test a mediation. I have my model, and I also determined that the best model is a more parsimonious one that constrains the auto regs and the cross lags. 

My question is: How do I now run the indirect effects to test mediation? A few of my A->B, B->C paths are significant, so I need to run several indirect effect paths. Is there code that anyone might be able to share with me to run those effects? 

Thank you so much!
Blake

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Cross-lagged mediation code question
parts: How do I now run the indirect effects to test mediation?

The same way you would in any other context.  Use the ":=" operator to specify the indirect effects of interest.  I assume you made equality constraints on AR and CL paths by using the same labels for multiple parameters. Those are the labels you use to define your indirect effects.
A few of my A->B, B->C paths are significant, so I need to run several indirect effect paths.

I'm not sure what you mean.  Equality constraints mean that (direct effect) parameters are equal over time.  By implication, any indirect effect is also equal over time, assuming it is constructed from direct effects that are equal over time. 

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
